affectedAssessments.assessment: Pneumatic is locally explained as powered by compressed air. Piston and cylinder are identified as a movable fitting part and its hollow chamber. Power stroke is explicitly linked to working stroke and to the part of travel when expanding gas drives the piston. Same phase is explained as remaining liquid or solid rather than changing state. These glosses resolve the apparatus/state vocabulary barrier without adding a valve model, engine cycle or apparatus detail.
affectedAssessments.conditionsRetained: Reservoir/supply/regulator control still conditions the near-isobaric approximation; compressibility alone still does not guarantee it. Pressure need not remain constant through the stroke. Smaller same-phase liquid/solid expansion is limited to this particular method and is not a gas-only rule for all engines.
affectedAssessments.childReadability: Definitions precede subsequent use; the mechanism, operating condition and examples are separated into short paragraphs. The new working-stroke explanation names what moves and connects the prose terminology to the already reviewed figure label without changing that label.

affectedAssessments.assessment: Rarefied is explained as relatively few molecules in a given space. Mean free path is the average travel distance between collisions with other molecules. The following paragraph compares that distance with container size before explaining wall-dominated collisions.
affectedAssessments.conditionsRetained: Engineering vacuum is still below atmospheric pressure, not the complete absence of molecules. The long-free-path wall-dominated condition remains a particular regime, not the definition of every vacuum. The text says molecular collisions are less frequent, not impossible.
affectedAssessments.childReadability: The average-distance gloss has its own paragraph and a clear referent in If this distance. Separating the general vacuum definition, glossary and conditional consequence resolves the original dense sentence.

affectedAssessments.assessment: Gas conduction is explained through molecular interactions; convection carries heat with moving gas. A separate paragraph states that radiation crosses the gap without gas and solid connecting parts still conduct heat. The imperfect-insulation conclusion and metal-refining application remain.
affectedAssessments.conditionsRetained: Removing gas reduces gas-mediated conduction/convection, not all heat transfer. Radiation and solid-path conduction are explicitly retained; no numerical heat-flow claim or perfect-insulation guarantee is added.
affectedAssessments.childReadability: Each mechanism has a direct explanatory clause or short sentence. The two paragraphs distinguish what removing gas reduces from what can remain.
